In this example, the variable limit $x$ is located on the lower limit. To apply FTC II, we prefer the variable to be on the upper limit. Using the properties of definite integrals, we can write

$$
h(x)={\int }_{x}^{3}{t}^{2}{e}^{3t}\,\text{d}t=-{\int }_{3}^{x}{t}^{2}{e}^{3t}\,\text{d}t.
$$

Therefore, by FTC II, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}{\int }_{x}^{3}{t}^{2}{e}^{3t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-{\int }_{3}^{x}{t}^{2}{e}^{3t}\,\text{d}t) \\  & =-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({\int }_{3}^{x}{t}^{2}{e}^{3t}\,\text{d}t) \\  & =-{x}^{2}{e}^{3x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the value of ${h}^{′}(2),$ we substitute $x=2$ in the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{′}(2) & =-{2}^{2}\cdot {e}^{3(2)} \\  & =-4{e}^{6}\end{aligned}
$$
